newsitem.title: UK: British 1997/98 beet crop gets off to flying start.
newsitem.headline: British 1997/98 beet crop gets off to flying start.

text.p: Britain has kicked off its 1997/98 sugar crop by drilling over a fifth of the total beet area of 170,000 hectares, an official at British Sugar said on Wednesday.
As of March 15 farmers had drilled 22 percent of the national area, compared with just four percent at the same stage in 1996/97, the official said.
"It is a good start. They've obviously taken advantage of the pleasant conditions that were around at the time," he said.
"But the weather (forecast) for this weekend is not so hot...a bit frosty."
Beet planting trials were held earlier this month.
Britain produced a record 1.48 million tonnes of sugar in white value terms from its 1996/97 beet crop.
The previous record was in 1992/93, when around 1,000 tonnes less sugar was produced.
